name: Balloon Selection
summary: Fingers on a multi-touch table steer a 3D spherical cursor above it, like a helium balloon on a string, for precise selection with resting hands.
howItWorks: Two adjacent fingers on the tabletop create the balloon. One finger (the anchor) moves it in the horizontal plane; the distance to a second finger sets its height, like pulling a string. A third finger changes the balloon's radius, and placing a finger next to the second one triggers selection of everything inside the balloon. The 3D task is split into a 2D and a 1D positioning task, and the hands rest on the surface.
advantages: Hands rest on the table, reducing hand tremor and arm fatigue.
In the study it was as fast as a tracked 3D wand and about three times less error-prone (5.5% vs 16.1%).
limitations: Works only in the volume above an interactive surface.
The balloon first appears at the surface, often hidden behind the scene.

relationships.note: Designed for selecting small objects in tabletop world-in-miniature models.
Both select with a 3D volume cursor.

review.notes: Added from the paper (Benko & Feiner, 3DUI 2007), coded from the full text in Oct 2026.
